app: Singpass (OpenCerts for education; native ISO-based Verifiable Digital Credentials in development)
takeup: 97% of residents hold Singpass (ASEAN report); 2,700+ services across 800+ public and private organisations. OpenCerts used by 20+ institutions. No population-scale VC figures yet.
ag: Government Technology Agency (GovTech): Singpass / National Digital Identity
sum: Singpass is an OIDC-based federated single sign-on and authentication platform, not a portable verifiable credential. It is used by government agencies (CPF, IRAS, HDB, MOH), banks (Myinfo-based KYC onboarding), insurers, telcos, utilities and car-sharing firms, and supports Sign with Singpass digital signing and in-person Verify via QR. OpenCerts provides blockchain-anchored education certificates. **Proposed:** native ISO/IEC 18013-5 aligned Verifiable Digital Credentials bootstrapped onto the Singpass base, targeting cross-border business registration and digital travel credentials.

app: Aadhaar (base identity), Aadhaar App / Wallet and DigiLocker (VC layer)
takeup: 1.43 billion Aadhaar numbers issued (base platform, ~90M authentications a day). VC layer: 50M+ Aadhaar Verifiable Credential downloads within six months, 200+ relying parties, 2M VC presentations.
leg: Aadhaar (Targeted Delivery of Financial and Other Subsidies, Benefits and Services) Act 2016 (amended 2019, 2024)
Information Technology Act 2000 (legal basis for DigiLocker)
ag: Ministry of Electronics and IT (MeitY): DigiLocker / NeGD
sum: India operates two layers. The base Aadhaar platform is **identity matching**: relying parties send an Aadhaar number plus biometric or OTP and UIDAI returns a yes/no or signed eKYC payload. It underpins Direct Benefit Transfer (USD ~54bn saved since 2013), PDS food and LPG subsidies, Jan Dhan banking, UPI, income tax e-filing and Digi Yatra. The newer **VC layer** issues SD-JWT VC and ISO mDoc credentials via OpenID4VCI/OpenID4VP for offline verification by finance, hospitality and social media relying parties, with DigiLocker issuing degrees, driving licences and PAN. **Proposed:** 20M VC presentations a day by 2032 and cross-border pilots with Bhutan, Thailand, Singapore, the Philippines, Ethiopia and the EU.

comps.s: Aadhaar VC (SD-JWT VC, ISO mDoc), DigiLocker signed documents

takeup: Formally launched to the public 10 Feb 2025; coverage projected at ~800,000 residents (near-universal) once the Ethereum migration completes; 40+ connected services.
leg: National Digital Identity Act of Bhutan 2023
ag: Department of Civil Registration and Census (DCRC), Ministry of Home Affairs
sum: The world's first national-scale self-sovereign identity system. Built on the W3C Verifiable Credentials Data Model with DIDs; anchored originally on Hyperledger Indy and Polygon, migrating to public Ethereum (proofs only, no personal data on-chain). Credentials are used by banks (account opening, Bank of Bhutan, BNB), telecoms (SIM registration), healthcare, education (academic certificates), transport and government e-services. Bhutan is exporting its open-source wallet architecture (e.g. Sierra Leone) and piloting cross-border recognition with India.

comps.s: Bhutan NDI wallet (W3C VC, DIDs on Ethereum)

app: Mobile ID (Mobile Resident Registration Card, Mobile Driver's Licence), also via Samsung Wallet
takeup: Nationwide availability for 52M citizens (March 2025). Confirmed issuance: 2.22M+ mobile ID cards via the Interior Ministry by 2024. Samsung Wallet reaches up to 17M domestic users (channel reach, not activations).
leg: Resident Registration Act (amended for mobile ID legal equivalence)
ag: Ministry of the Interior and Safety (MOIS)
Presidential Committee on Digital Platform Government
sum: A blockchain-based DID architecture chosen to address surveillance concerns, with the mobile driver's licence the credential most comparable to ISO/IEC 18013-5. Selective disclosure supports age checks without revealing date of birth. Integrated with 15 major banks for account opening and lending, police and government office ID checks, retail and hospitality age verification, domestic air travel and city benefit programmes (Busan multi-child family benefits). Mobile Foreign Residence Cards added January 2025.
links: Ministry of the Interior and Safety

app: myID / AGDIS (SSO); DVS and NDLFRS (identity matching); state digital licence apps (Queensland Digital Licence, Service NSW, Service Victoria)
takeup: 7M+ Australians hold a digital driver's licence: NSW ~4.5M, Victoria ~1.8M, Queensland ~1.2M (ISO 18013-5 compliant). National VC totals are not centrally published.
leg: Digital ID Act 2024 (Commonwealth): voluntary accreditation for OIDC-based identity exchange (myID), not the basis for state licences
Digital ID Rules 2024 and Accreditation Rules
State transport legislation (e.g. Transport Operations (Road Use Management) Act 1995 Qld; Photo Card Act 2005 NSW)
Identity Verification Services Act 2023 (DVS, Face Verification Service, NDLFRS)
ag: Queensland Department of Transport and Main Roads
Service NSW / Department of Customer Service
sum: A hybrid of three models. **Identity matching:** the Document Verification Service (DVS) and Face Verification Service check identity documents and photos against issuing registries, drawing on the National Driver Licence Facial Recognition Solution (NDLFRS), with NEVDIS (run by Austroads) holding national driver licence and vehicle data; used by banks, telcos and government for KYC. **Single sign-on:** myID and the Australian Government Digital ID System (AGDIS) provide federated login to myGov, ATO, Centrelink and accredited private providers under the Digital ID Act 2024. **Verifiable credentials:** states issue mobile driver licences, with Queensland fully conformant with ISO/IEC 18013-5 and all jurisdictions agreeing in June 2024 to converge on ISO 18013-5/23220; credentials include licences, photo ID, marine and fishing licences, QBCC and White Card, Working with Children Checks and the NSW digital birth certificate. **Proposed:** a national Digital Trust Service and full ISO alignment across remaining states.

comps.s: Document Verification Service, NDLFRS face matching, NEVDIS
myID, Australian Government Digital ID System (AGDIS), myGov

NZ Transport Agency Waka Kotahi (driver licence)

The digital driver licence is being built on ISO 18013-5 and ISO 23220 aligned with Austroads, and NZ Verify already verifies inbound mDLs from Queensland and 16 US states. Accredited providers include banks and identity services. **Proposed:** progressive issuance of government credentials into the govt.nz wallet through 2026, with RealMe retained for SSO login and the DISTF governing private-sector reuse (e.g. eKYC banking credentials).

comps.s: RealMe verified identity, DIA Confirmation Service

Used for health insurance (My Number insurance card), tax filing (e-Tax), benefits, convenience-store certificate printing, bank and securities KYC, and since March 2025 the driver's licence. **Proposed:** mDoc-format credential issuance and a new Myna App in 2026.

comps.s: JPKI X.509 certificates on My Number Card and smartphone

app: National Online Identity Authentication Public Service ("network number" app); CTID; RealDID (pilot); proposed distributed digital identity framework
takeup: Network number: voluntary opt-in since 15 July 2025, no official adoption figures. RealDID: pilot since December 2023, no published user figures. Distributed digital identity framework: draft only (public comment closed 18 July 2026).
leg: Measures for the National Online Identity Authentication Public Service (2025)
Regulations on Promoting the Interoperability and Interrecognition of Distributed Digital Identity Applications (CAC draft, 18 June 2026; consultation closed 18 July 2026)
ag: Ministry of Public Security (MPS) and its First Research Institute (CTID)
Cyberspace Administration of China (CAC / State Internet Information Office)
State Information Center / BSN (national blockchain network)
sum: Today China runs **identity matching** and **SSO**. The network number is a government online identity token verified by NFC read of the resident identity card against the MPS registry (online only), alongside CTID registry checks and the National Government Service Platform SSO. **Blockchain VC (pilot):** RealDID, launched in December 2023 on the national blockchain network with the MPS First Research Institute, issues decentralised identifiers linked to real-name verification for login and data authorisation. **Proposed:** in June 2026 the CAC published draft regulations for state-backed "distributed digital identities" built on the national blockchain network. Each identity combines an identifier, a key, verifiable credentials and verifiable claims, with selective disclosure. Authoritative identity authentication institutions register users through "identity chains" and issue a real-name identity certificate, and VC issuers and relying institutions are defined roles. Intended uses are account management, login authentication and data authorisation across individuals, organisations, devices and goods. The draft is silent on privacy safeguards and how surveillance and national-security access would be handled.

comps.s: MPS / NCIIC identity checks, CTID platform, network number
RealDID on the national blockchain network (BSN, MPS First Research Institute)
Distributed digital identity framework (CAC draft regulations): DIDs and VCs on the national blockchain network

sum: Russia combines **single sign-on** and **identity matching**, with a growing biometric layer. Gosuslugi, the state services portal, authenticates citizens through ESIA (the Unified Identification and Authentication System) and is used by government and banks. The **Unified Biometric System** holds citizens' face and voice biometrics under Federal Law 572-FZ; banks, retailers and Moscow transport (face-pay turnstiles) verify people against it. The **Max** app, a state-backed messenger and super-app launched in 2025 with VK and required to be pre-installed on devices sold in Russia, carries a digital ID with name, date of birth, passport, tax and social insurance numbers, registration address and biometrics. It is presented as a QR code that discloses only the details needed for each situation. This is not a standards-based verifiable credential. Max ID is used for retail age checks, cultural and transport concessions for students, pensioners, large families and people with disabilities, and hotel check-in pilots: guests without a Russian passport at hotels of more than 50 rooms must use it, with rollout to several thousand hotels within a year. It is now open to teenagers aged 14 and over. Apple removed Max from its App Store in June 2026 citing sanctions. **Proposed:** wider biometric use in transport, retail, public services and online age verification, and biometric identification in prisons under Bill 460-9. Commentators raise concerns over mass surveillance, metadata sharing with authorities and camera databases used against political dissent.

sum: Paraguay combines **single sign-on** and **identity matching**. A national e-government platform launched in 2018 gives online access to public services. Since Law 7177/2023, digital versions of the national identity card and driver's licence issued through it are legally equivalent to the physical documents. The standards behind these credentials (for example ISO 18013-5) are not published, so they are treated here as registry-backed rather than verifiable credentials. The Cédula de Identidad is issued by the Policía Nacional's Departamento de Identificaciones; Paraguay is the only Mercosur country that has not separated civil document issuance from the police. Banks, financial entities and payment providers verify customers against this registry under AML/CFT rules supervised by SEPRELAD and the Banco Central del Paraguay. **Concerns (TEDIC, 2024):** the digital ID law lacks adequate implementing regulation, there was no data protection law, privacy policies cite repealed laws, the state acknowledged sharing digital ID data with Google Analytics, and biometric collection needs limits. TEDIC's recommendations include risk assessments, transparency, regulation, inclusive access, alignment with international standards and stronger biometric safeguards.
